content:
{D}Sing {G}Ho! for a brave and a gallant ship
with a fair and a favourin' {C}breeze,
with a {G}bully crew and a {e}captain, too,
{a}to carry me over the {D7}seas,
to {G}carry me over the seas, my boys,
To my true love far a{C}way.
For I'm {G}takin' a trip on a {e}government ship
ten {a}thousand {D}miles a{G}way.

So blow the winds, heigh-ho!
A roving I will {C}go,
I'll {G}stay no more on {e}England's shore
to {a}hear the music {D7}play.
I'm {G}off on the morning train and
I won't be back {C}again.
For I'm {G}takin' a trip on a {e}government ship
ten {a}thousand {D}miles a{G}way.  

My true love, she was beautiful,
my true love she was young;
Her eyes were like two diamonds bright
and silvery was her tongue
and silvery was her tongue, me boys,
as the big ship sailed away 
And she said: "Will you remember me
ten thousand miles away?"

Oh, dark and dismal was the day
when last I saw me Meg.
She'd a government band around each hand
and another one 'round her leg.
And another one 'round her leg, me boys,
as the big ship left the bay
"Farewell" said she, "remember me,
ten thousand miles away." 

Well, I wish I was bosun bold
or even a bombadier,
I'd build a boat and away I'd float
and straight to my true love steer
And straight to my true love steer, me boys,
where the dancing dolphins play,
where the whales and sharks have all their larks,
ten thousand miles away.

Oh, the sun may shine through the London fog
or the river run quite clear,
or the ocean's brine turn into wine
or I forget my beer
Or I forget my beer, me boys,
or the landlord's quarter-day;
But I'll never forget my own true love,
ten thousand miles away!
title: Ten thousand miles away
